lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: That's the widow they sent away from Caesarea.

lines.speaker: dockworker2
lines.text: Esther's girl? Coming home with one bundle and no husband.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: Keep your voice down. She's looking this way.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. One foot on the dock and Joppa already knows me. Fast town.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Little loaf. You came.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Silas. You're the only one on this dock who's said my name... well. Nearly my name.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Jonah sailed from this very dock, you know. Every runaway in Israel does. Now, that reminds me—

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: I'm not running, Silas. I've run out of places. Take me to Savta's bakehouse.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Ah. About the bakehouse, little loaf... best you see it for yourself.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Boards on the door. Weeds in the step. Savta would have chased those weeds with a broom.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Three months shut. Nobody had the heart to open it. Or the nerve. It was always hers.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. Then I'll start with the doorway. A baker who can't reach her own oven isn't much of a baker.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: That's Esther's chin you've got. Now, that reminds me of the year the fish swam backward—

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Silas. Hold this board.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Holding. It was a cold year, mind you. The fish were as confused as anyone.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: There. The door opens. It still smells like her in here. Barley and smoke.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Come up to the roof before the light goes. She left something there she wanted you to see.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Here. Esther's prayer corner. Every morning before the oven, she sat right on that mat.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: It's her kitchen in miniature. Barley sheaves, jars, a little tray... all laid out in rows.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: She'd set two sheaves together and say, 'Small things joined make bigger things, Silas.'

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: And you'd say?

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: I'd say, 'Is there bread yet?' Forty years. She never once threw the tray at me.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: She prayed here for me. Didn't she. Even after what Caesarea said.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Every dawn, by name. And she told me: 'When my girl comes, tell her to look in the oven niche.'

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: The oven niche? Silas, what did she leave in there?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: A potsherd, tucked behind the ash. That's Savta's hand. She wrote to me.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: My Naomi. If you are reading this, you came home, and I am already Home.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: Don't cry on the dough — it makes it salty.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: I know what they said about you in Caesarea. I never believed a word.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: Fear will tell you to hide in this kitchen. Don't.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: "There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear." (1 John 4:18)

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: Open the shutters. — your Savta

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Too late, Savta. I'm already crying on things.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Open the shutters. Hm. That takes more love than fear. Start small, Naomi.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: There's a small person under my kneading table. Small persons usually knock.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: I'm Joy! I came in the back. The boards are loose. Are you the bread lady?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: I'm Naomi. Though lately I'd answer to Mara.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: Is it true you were sent away? Why? Were you bad?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: That's what Papa says when he doesn't want to answer. The ladies at the well said lots more.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: I'm sure they did. What do you want, Joy-who-came-in-the-back?

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: Honey cake! Esther always saved me the corner piece.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: No honey yet. No fire yet, either. But come back when the oven's lit, and we'll see.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: I'll come back every day! I'm very good at coming back.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Catch, you stubborn thing. Fifty years you lit for her. Light once for me.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: There! It's caught. Her oven still draws.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Smoke from Esther's chimney! Half the dock stopped hauling nets to stare.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Flatbread for the crews, Silas. Warm. Take it before I lose my nerve.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Mm. Oh, little loaf. That's her bread. That's her bread exactly.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: It's a little thick at the edge.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: I've told the whole dock you bake like Esther. Twice. Some of them three times.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: You told them before you tasted it?

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: A fisherman knows what's in the net before he pulls it. Mostly. There was one year—

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. If the whole dock knows, so does the well. I wonder who knocks first.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: So it's true! Esther's girl, home at last. And so thin, dear. Grief does suit some women.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Zilpah. What can I bake for you?

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: A flatbread and a little flour. So brave of you to bake here, where everyone remembers you.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: Caesarea must have been grand. All those fine Roman houses. Did you see inside many?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: Oh, I don't ask for myself. I'm only saying what people are saying, dear.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: People say a great deal for folk who weren't there.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Patience, Naomi. And peace enough not to bite.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Your bread, Zilpah. Still warm. That's a lovely shawl. Whoever made it had kind hands.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: It... yes. Well. I'll tell them at the well you were civil. They'll be so surprised.

lines.speaker: demas
lines.text: Gather close, friends, gather close! News from up the coast, fresh as this morning's catch.

lines.speaker: demas
lines.text: A tale of a widow from Caesarea. Young. Clever with her hands. And with Roman friends.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: Roman friends? What sort of friends?

lines.speaker: demas
lines.text: Ah, who can say? I only tell what the road tells me. Her husband's own mother sent her away.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: And now there's a widow from Caesarea baking our bread.

lines.speaker: demas
lines.text: Did I name a name? I named no name! A teller of tales only tells. You do the adding up.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: My basket was empty by noon yesterday. Today nobody has stopped. Not one.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: The fish-seller said her mama won't let her buy your bread now. That's silly. It's good bread.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: It's the same bread it was yesterday, Joy. Only the story changed.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: There's a man on my wall with a mallet. I didn't hire a man with a mallet.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: That's Papa! I told him your shutters hang like broken wings. He builds boats. Shutters are easy.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Hinge pins were rusted through. They'll hold now.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Thank you. What do I owe you? I can't pay much this week. You may have heard why.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Nothing owed. I don't listen at the market.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. Everyone in Joppa wants something from me. A story, mostly. And you want nothing.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Lower latch sticks. Lift, then push.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: Papa doesn't talk much. Not since Mama died. She died in the sea.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: People say things about that too. Papa says we don't answer. Is that why you say 'Hm'?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: ...Yes, little one. I think it might be.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Little loaf? That's a full basket. I thought nobody was buying.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Nobody is. So nobody's paying. The night crews still have to eat, Silas.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: We heard about you. I've no coin for a Caesarea widow's bread.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Good, because it isn't for sale. It's warm, and the wind is cold. Take two.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: ...Why would you feed men who talk about you?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: My grandmother fed this dock for fifty years. I doubt she liked all of you either.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Ha! She did not. She told me so weekly. Eat, lads, eat!

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: One basket doesn't change a story, Silas. I know that.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: No. But a man chews slower than he talks. Gives him time to think. Go home, rest.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: That brick by the oven moved. It never moved when I was a girl. Something's behind it.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Another shard. She knew I'd lean on this wall when I was tired.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: Every morning for fifty years I lit that oven in the dark, not knowing if anyone would buy a single loaf.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: Someone always came.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: "It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not." (Lamentations 3:22)

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: "They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness." (Lamentations 3:23)

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: The well remembers everything, little one. Go and listen. — your Savta

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Someone always came. Hm. Then I light it again tomorrow, in the dark.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: But the well? What does the well remember that she couldn't tell me herself?

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: The shutters are open! All of them! You can smell the bread from the boatyard!

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: New shelf, swept floor, clean ash. Savta would still find a crumb somewhere.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: Two loaves. My crew says the free bread was better than what we pay for elsewhere.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: You're... buying? With the whole street watching?

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: Let them watch. A man can't eat a story.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Three customers before noon! I counted. Well, two and a goat. But the goat looked interested.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: A loaf for supper. And I'll pay for this one. The shutters were a gift.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. Then the honey cake is a gift too. For your daughter. She's waited longer than anyone.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: The corner piece?!

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: ...Thank you, Naomi.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Last loaves out, Joy. Then we bank the fire. A good day. I'd forgotten what those feel like.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: Naomi, someone's at the door. It's Elder Amos. He looks all white, like flour.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Elder? Sit, sit. You're shaking. Here's the bread for the widows' table, it's all ready—

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: Well now. Well now, child. Keep the bread. I don't know that they'll take it from my hands.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Take it from... Amos, what's happened?

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: The widows' fund. Every coin the believers gathered. The chest is empty.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Empty? Stolen? Who would rob widows?

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: That is what the whole well is asking. And they have already settled on a name.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Whose name, Elder?

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: Mine.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Savta said the well remembers everything. Hm. It also repeats everything, loudly.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: Every coin the widows had, dear. Gone. And only one man in Joppa kept the key to that chest.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: Elder Amos? He prayed over my boy when he had the fever.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: Such a kind man. So forgetful, too. One does wonder what else he forgot to mention.

lines.speaker: dockworker2
lines.text: They say he was seen at the moneylender's gate. What's an elder want there?

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: I accuse no one. I'm only saying what people are saying, dear.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: People said plenty about me, Zilpah. Not one of them asked me first.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: And we never did hear your side, did we? Careful, dear. Loyalty to a thief looks so poorly.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: This well is cracked from lip to rope. Somebody ought to mend it. Hm. I suppose I'm somebody.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Little loaf? That's mortar on your sleeves, not flour. Have you changed trades?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: The lip is cracked clean through, Silas. One more winter and it falls in the water.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Forty years I've leaned on that stone. Now, that reminds me of the year the well ran salty—

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Silas. Hold this wedge.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Holding. It was the same year my cousin married a goatherd. Unrelated, mind you.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. The woman Joppa whispers about, mending the place it whispers. Savta would laugh.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: She'd laugh, then hand you more mortar. There. Sound as a millstone.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: The stone's the easy part. The rope's rotten too. And nobody's seen Elder Amos since yesterday.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: No lamp in his window last night. In forty years I've not seen that window dark.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Dark? Silas, mind the mortar. I'm going up there.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Elder? The door was open. You're burning up. How long have you lain here alone?

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: Well now. A day? Two? The fever keeps poor count, child.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Drink this. Slowly. Then tell me about the chest, and I'll tell the well to hush.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: The chest is empty. That much is true. I'll not pretend otherwise.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Then where did it go? One word from you and this ends by noon.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: It is not only my word to give. There's another's shame bound up in it.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: They're calling you a thief, Amos!

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: Ha. An old vine gets called worse by the goats. It bears anyway.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: But I confess, child, I have no peace tonight. Not for my name. For the flock.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. I kept a promise once, and it cost me dearly. I know that look. Rest. I'll stay.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: Nobody came, Naomi. It's meeting night and the room is all empty.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: No lamps lit, no bread broken. Three days of whispering, and a whole family scatters.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Benches are split. Two legs gone on this one.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Can you mend them?

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Already measuring.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: I found the lamps! They're dusty. One has a spider. I named him Jonah.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Jonah can stay if he sits quietly. Trim the wicks, Joy. We're lighting every one.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: And if nobody comes, little loaf? Folk don't like to sit in a house the well has judged.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Then we sit here ourselves. Savta lit her oven in the dark for fifty years. Someone always came.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: Well now. I hear benches. Is that my flock, or very organized thieves?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Go back to sleep, Elder. It's only your family.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: A shepherd who can't account for the purse should lay down the staff. For his own good, dear.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: He hasn't denied it. Three days now. An innocent man would shout.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: He has a fever, not a guilty tongue. He can barely lift a cup.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: How convenient a fever can be. People are saying the flock needs a new elder by the Sabbath.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. The bucket stone rocks. Let them talk. I'll lift it and set it level.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: A potsherd, face down in the damp. Savta. You hid one even here.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: Half this town has decided a man is guilty before breakfast. I have done it too, God forgive me.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: "He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him." (Proverbs 18:13)

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: Hear the whole matter, Naomi. Especially from the ones who aren't talking. — your Savta

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: The ones who aren't talking. Everyone at this well is talking, Savta.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: ...So who isn't at the well?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: You're early, Caleb. I meant to hang the rope before the well woke up and had opinions.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Brought ship's line. Tarred. It won't rot.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: A boat builder's rope on a town well. It'll outlast us all.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Someone's coming. The lane behind the potter's.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: A woman with two jars and her shawl pulled low. That's the widow Hannah. At this hour?

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Every dawn. Before the others. Since the new moon.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: She saw us. She's turned back, Caleb. With both jars empty.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Folk who walk the long way round have a reason.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: The ones who aren't talking. Hm. A widow who'd sooner go thirsty than be seen.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Knot it tight. I'll leave a full jar at the end of her lane. No questions. Not yet.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: I'm helping! I scrubbed the whole trough. And my tunic. And a goat, a little.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: The goat thanks you. You've been gone all morning. Where does a Joy go?

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: Playing knucklebones with Eli and Ben. Hannah's boys. They cheat, but nicely.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: The big boys said the elder is a thief. And Ben got so angry his ears went red.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Angry? What did Ben say, Joy? Exactly as he said it.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: He said, 'Don't you call him that. The elder saved us.' Then Eli pulled him away quick.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Saved them. From what?

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: I asked! Eli said it's a secret, and their mama cries when they say it.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: Was it bad to tell you? At the well everybody tells everything.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: This once, little one, you carried something true. But we don't pour it in the well. It stays here.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: The elder saved us. And a mother who hides at dawn. Hm. I think I owe Hannah some bread.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hannah? It's Naomi, the baker. I've no questions in this basket. Only bread.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: You shouldn't be seen at my door. They'll say things.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: They already say things about me. One more won't crowd the pot.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: You left water by my lane. Three mornings. Nobody else even looked.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: I know what it is to take the long way round. I'm not here to drag anything out of you.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: My husband left a debt. The creditor came at the new moon. He came for Eli and Ben.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Your sons? Into servitude?

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: For years. I ran to the elder in the night and begged. I had nothing. Nothing.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: He paid it all by morning. From the chest. He said he'd put it back before anyone missed it.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: Then the fever took him, and the well took his name. And I hid, because I was ashamed.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: And he never once said your name. Not even to me.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: He kept faith with me. I've kept none with him. Naomi... I don't know if I'm brave enough.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Little loaf, look up from that bench. Tell me my old eyes aren't lying.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Elder Amos! On your own feet! You ought to be in bed!

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: Well now. The fever left in the night. It found me poor company. May I try your bench?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: You're its first sitter. Mind the left end, the pegs are fresh.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: I owe you an answer, child. I'd have given it sooner, but the fever took my legs first.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: This is a bill of sale. My vineyard plot, the one my father planted. Agreed before I fell ill.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Your vineyard? Amos, that's all the land you have.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: A vine is for giving fruit, child. This one gives it all at once. The chest will be full again.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Then show this at the well! One look and the whispering stops.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: And when they ask what I spent it on? I'll not buy my name back with another's shame.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. What if she wants to give it? Her own telling, her own choice.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: ...You know. Well now. Then it is hers to choose, and no one is to push her. Not even kindly.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Base course is the last of it. This stone's been weeping for years.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Then out it comes. A well that leaks at the root isn't mended, only dressed up.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Naomi. Something's mortared in behind it.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: A shard. Carved, not inked. She meant this one to last under water. Oh, Savta.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: I carved this one for the well because it is the loudest place in Joppa.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: "A froward man soweth strife: and a whisperer separateth chief friends." (Proverbs 16:28)

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: A rumor is a crack in a jar. It doesn't break all at once. It just leaks until nothing is left.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: Mend what you can. — your Savta

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Chief friends. Amos and his flock. Hannah and every woman at this well.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Stone's ready to go back. You'll keep the shard?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: I'll keep it. Set the stone true, Caleb. Hannah said she'd come at noon.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: If her courage holds. Hm. Mend what you can.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: The square does look fine, dear. A pity a man's name can't be mortared so easily.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: Please. May I speak? I have never spoken at this well in my life.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: A creditor came for my sons. I begged the elder in the night. He paid the debt from the chest.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: He told no one, to spare me. And I let you call him a thief, because I was ashamed. Forgive me.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: He saved her boys? And we had him robbing widows...

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: Well now. The chest is owed, and it will be paid. My vineyard is sold. Here is the bill.

lines.speaker: dockworker2
lines.text: Elder, I said things. At this very stone. I'd take them back if words came back.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: Words don't, son. But you came back, and that's the better catch. There's nothing owed me.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: I told you nothing, and silence leaves room for guessing. That part is mine. The rest I forgive, all of it.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Zilpah hasn't said a word. First time since I came home. She's holding her shawl very tight.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: Zilpah. Come on meeting night, if you like. There's a bench mended, and room on it.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: She didn't answer. But she didn't leave, either. Hm. Mend what you can.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: A full basket and a full chest, little loaf! The elder's vineyard coin came in this morning.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: And the room was full last night. Joy counted twice, in case anyone had sneaked out.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Now, that reminds me of the year— hold. Who's that on the toll steps? That's no fisherman.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: Fine cloak. Roman toll seal on his belt. The new collector. Hide your catch, lads.

lines.speaker: dockworker2
lines.text: They say this one counts every fin.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: That walk. I know that walk. No. No, it can't—

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Little loaf! Your basket! The bread's all over the dock!

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Still dropping things when you're startled. Hello, Sister.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Marcus.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: There's your toll, collector. Right at your feet. Rome can have that share for nothing.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: You missed the sandal. Most men do. Five baskets, I make it. Next boat.

lines.speaker: dockworker2
lines.text: Baker. He called you 'Sister' last night. You know that man?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. I know flatbread. Yours is going cold. Take it.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Little loaf. That's Esther's grandson on those steps. You can't 'Hm' him into the sea.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Eight years without a word, Silas. Then he comes home wearing Rome's seal. I can try.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: No toll on bread, baker. Pass freely. We've never met, after all. Have we, Sister?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: He looks thin under that fine cloak. No. I'm not looking. I've bread to carry.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Esther wrote to that boy every month. I sent each shard up the coast with any boat that would carry one.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Every month? And he never answered her. Not once?

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Not once. And the last she wrote the week she took ill. I never did find where she put it.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Savta's basket of writing shards. Under the counter all this time, and I only took from the top.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: After Father died, Marcus stopped talking. One morning his bed was empty. He was eighteen.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: He thought Joppa pitied him. A proud boy would sooner be hated than pitied.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: I asked at every gate. Savta only said, 'He knows the way home.' Eight years, Silas!

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Here. At the very bottom. This one isn't blank. It has his name on it.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: Marcus. I wrote you every month. You never answered, and I never stopped.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: When you come back — and you will — know this:

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: "But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion," (Luke 15:20)

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: "and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him." (Luke 15:20)

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: Nobody has to earn their way back to this table. — your Savta

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: She never stopped. I stopped years ago. Hm. This isn't mine to keep, is it.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: It's got his name on it, little loaf. But I'd not hand it over on the open dock. Not this week.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Three posts rotted through at the waterline. One good swell and the whole dock walks off.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Then we brace them today. Bread for every man who lifts a beam. Who's with me?

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: For your bread, baker, gladly. But not while he stands on the toll steps counting us.

lines.speaker: dockworker2
lines.text: Mend the dock so he can tax it finer? Let him haul the timber. Or let it rot.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Don't stop on my account. A sound dock lands more fish. I'm very fond of fish.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Must you make it worse every time you open your mouth?

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: It's a gift, Sister. Ask anyone. I'll take my seal up the quay. Mend your dock.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: Is he the bad man? He doesn't look bad. He looks like he forgot to eat.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. Hold the mallet for your father, Joy.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: He's gone. They'll work now. ...He looked back twice, Naomi.

lines.speaker: demas
lines.text: Gather close, friends, gather close! Today, a tale of a fine cloak and a Roman seal.

lines.speaker: demas
lines.text: He counts your catch to the last fin. And what he takes, friends? Does it all reach Caesarea?

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: Toll went up at the new year, and now he comes to count it. I knew it. He's lining that cloak with our fish.

lines.speaker: demas
lines.text: And at night! A lamp in the old boat shed. A pen, scratching. Whose names does he write?

lines.speaker: dockworker2
lines.text: Names? For Rome? My cousin sold two baskets off the back steps and never paid toll...

lines.speaker: demas
lines.text: Did I say Rome? I said a lamp and a pen! A teller of tales only tells. You do the adding up.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: And such a familiar chin on that young man, dear. I'm only saying what people are saying.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: He tells it well. That's the trouble. Eight years gone, and I can't swear it isn't true.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: I don't know my own brother well enough to defend him. What does he write at night?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Twelve new planks, Silas. You can reach your boat without swimming. Say something about fish.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: No story today, little loaf. Sit down by me.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: No story? Now you're frightening me.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Your brother stopped by my boat at dusk. Asked after my nets, my catch. Friendly. My lads saw.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Now they say I'm selling names to the toll man. Two of them won't sail with me tomorrow.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: On Demas's word? A lamp and a pen, and a whole crew scatters?

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: On nobody's word. That's how it works. So I'm asking you plain: keep him away from my crew.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: You carried Savta's letters to him for years. Now you want me to turn him away for you.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: For my crew. They've children to feed. It's the hardest thing I've ever asked of Esther's girl.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. I'll tell him. And then I'll hate that I did.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Last of the weed off the slipway. A boat could come up this without breaking its back.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Wind's turning. Something's blown down off the quay. There, in the shallows.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Papyrus. It'll be pulp in a moment. Got it. Hm. Columns of figures. This is from a toll roll.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: The collector's hand?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: My brother's hand. That crooked tail on every letter. Father used to scold him for it.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Boat by boat, day by day. And beside each one, two numbers. Caleb, they don't match.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Two counts for one catch.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: One count for the crews and one for himself. Two sets of numbers. What else is that for?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Demas was right. I wanted so badly for Demas to be wrong.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: A page isn't a man. I've had a tale told about me off less than that.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hear the whole matter. Savta wrote me that once. Hm. Then I'll hear it from him. Tonight.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: A cloak for a blanket and a net for a pillow. Rome's collector sleeps in a boat shed?

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: The lodging is cheap and the neighbors don't spit. What do you want, Sister?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: This blew into the harbor. Two columns, Marcus. Two numbers for every boat. Explain it.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: You've heard Demas. I cheat, I inform, I sour the milk. Pick one and go home.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: I nearly did. Then I found Silas's boat. Nine baskets landed. You wrote six, and six is what he paid.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: The second column is smaller. Every line. You're writing down less than they land.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Caesarea raised the rate at the new year. Half these boats would have been sold by summer.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: So I enter less, they pay less, and I make up the box from my wages. The box is never short.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: All your wages? That's why you sleep here. That's why you look half starved.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Don't make me good. I took the seal for the cloak and the coin. I just can't watch them sink.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: They spit at you and you let them. ...This was at the bottom of Savta's basket. It has your name on it.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: 'Nobody has to earn their way back.' She would say that. ...Nomi. Tell no one. If the crews hear, Caesarea hears.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: Leave the fish table, baker. A boat from Caesarea, and scribes on the plank. That's no merchant.

lines.speaker: collector
lines.text: I am chief collector for this coast. Joppa's toll roll is to be examined. Three days, every boat.

lines.speaker: collector
lines.text: I count the landings myself, at this table. Collector, bring me your roll at the third dawn.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: It will be ready, sir.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Three days of his counting against weeks of yours. Marcus, he'll see it.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: By the second morning, I'd think. He has the look of a man who can add.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: There's a grain ship for Cyprus on tomorrow's tide. Nobody knows me in Cyprus.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: You'd run. Again.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: What would you have me do, Sister? Say it to his face and lose the little I have left?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: I can't say it for you. I wouldn't if I could. But I'd sooner have a brother than a collector.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: ...The tide's at dawn, Nomi. Don't wait up.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: New net racks up by first light. The Cyprus ship cleared the rocks at dawn. I didn't look who was aboard.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Little loaf. Look to the fish table. That's your brother standing at it, roll in hand.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Sir. Before you count another boat. The roll is false, and I am the one who falsified it.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I entered every catch smaller than it landed. What the box lacked, I paid in from my own wages.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: The crews never knew. They paid what I asked. If there is a fault here, it has one name. Mine.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: Smaller? He wrote us down smaller, and paid the rest himself? ...And we spat at him.

lines.speaker: collector
lines.text: The box is whole. I cannot charge these boats for a debt already paid. That much is plain.

lines.speaker: collector
lines.text: But a man who writes a false roll cannot carry a seal. Your post is ended, your wages forfeit.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Take the seal. It never did sit right on my belt.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: No seal, no wages, no post. And he's standing straighter than he has all week.

lines.speaker: dockworker2
lines.text: Baker... your own brother. And what have we been saying about him?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: There. Oil in the lantern and a flame that holds. The dock hasn't had a light since I came home.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Very fine. It'll light my way to the boat shed. If the shed will still have me.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: Marcus. I spat at your feet every morning, and you were paying my toll. I was wrong.

lines.speaker: dockworker2
lines.text: I said worse than he did, in the market, to anyone who'd stand still. Can you forgive it?

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: And I turned Esther's grandson from my boat on a market tale. That one's mine to carry, lad.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: I wore the seal and the sneer both. I gave you every reason. ...Yes. It's forgiven. All of it.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: I'm short two hands and long on nets. Cold, wet work, and the pay is fish. Will you sail with us?

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Me? I can't tell a sprat from a sandal.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Every runaway sails from Joppa. Some sail home.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: ...Nomi. Say something sharp, quick, before I disgrace myself in front of my crew.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. You'll smell of fish. I'll bake for you anyway.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: My old net box, little loaf. Lid's split, hinge is rope. Now, that reminds me of the year—

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: The fish that swam backward? I've crewed two days and heard it four times.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hush, both of you. There's a shard wedged under the bottom board. Silas, that's Savta's hand.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Forty years she borrowed twine out of that box. I never once looked under the boards.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: For both my grandchildren, who are stubborn like their grandfather.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: When the whole harbor is against you, remember who stands with you.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: "The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust;" (Psalm 18:2)

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: "my buckler, and the horn of my salvation, and my high tower." (Psalm 18:2) — your Savta

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Both. She wrote 'both.' She put me in it before I'd even come home.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: She knew the harbor would turn on each of us. And she knew we'd be standing here together.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: She told me once, 'Mind that box, Silas.' I thought she meant the twine.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Sound lid, new hinge. That's the last of the dock mended. I almost don't trust the quiet.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: The whole dock's done! I ran it end to end and nothing wobbled. I ran it six times!

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Posts are sound. Planks are true. It'll stand a storm.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: And my new hand caught a fish today! A small one. It may have been unwell. But a fish!

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: It was a fine fish, old man. Nomi, tell him it was a fine fish.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: It was a fish. Sit, all of you. The bread's warm, and for once nobody here is whispering.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: Demas has it in the market already. The toll man who paid our tolls. He tells it well.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. He always does. One day I'd like him to ask first.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Wait. Listen. Someone's crying out on the upper street.

lines.speaker: dockworker2
lines.text: Baker! Come quick! It's Tabitha, who sews for the widows. She's collapsed!

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Tabitha? She's clothed half the widows in Joppa. Esther's dearest friend...

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: All these weeks home, and I never once climbed the hill to see her. Marcus, the basket. I'm going up.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Tabitha? It's Naomi, Esther's granddaughter. I brought bread. It's still warm.

lines.speaker: tabitha
lines.text: Esther's Naomi. Come in, come in. You have her hands.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. Flour to the elbow, you mean. Lie still. Hannah says you fell at the loom.

lines.speaker: tabitha
lines.text: I was tired, that is all. The tunics for the widows are not finished.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Six of them, cut and laid out. You've been sewing with a fever?

lines.speaker: tabitha
lines.text: Winter does not wait for me to be well. Naomi, will you finish them?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: I bake. My stitches wander like a goat on a hill.

lines.speaker: tabitha
lines.text: Then the widows will have warm coats with wandering stitches. The basket is by the loom.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: She made the coat on my back, Naomi. And both my boys' tunics. She never took a coin.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Then I'll finish them. Rest, Tabitha. I'll bring the first one to show you tomorrow.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: She's asleep already. Her hand is so hot. Hannah... send for me if anything changes.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: One sleeve done by lamplight. Crooked, but done. I'll take it up to her with the morning bread.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: Naomi. Elder Amos is at the door. He isn't saying 'well now.' He isn't saying anything.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: Child. Put the basket down. Tabitha died in the night.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: No. I was to show her the sleeve. I told her tomorrow.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: The women have washed her and laid her in the upper room. Half of Joppa is on the hill, weeping.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: She made my tunic. The too-big one. She said I'd grow into it. Who'll tell her when I do?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Come here, little one. ...I don't know. I don't know.

lines.speaker: simon
lines.text: Forgive me. I'm Simon, the tanner. Folk are walking in from the villages, and the hill has no room.

lines.speaker: simon
lines.text: My house is by the sea. People don't come to it. But the yard is wide, and the gate is open.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: Well now. That is kindly offered, Simon. And kindly needed.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. Then it wants sweeping, and they'll want bread. Joy, bring the broom. We can do that much.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: This is the coat she made me the winter my husband died. Look at the hem. Not a stitch has slipped.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: My mother's shawl. Tabitha brought it herself, in the rain, and wouldn't stay for thanks.

lines.speaker: dockworker2
lines.text: Every widow in this room is wearing her work. They keep holding it up, as if she might see.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: And six tunics still pinned on the table. I said I'd finish them. Where's her basket?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Under the thread, a potsherd. That's Savta's hand. Here, in Tabitha's basket?

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: Tabitha and I made a pact: whoever went first would leave something for the other's girl.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: If you are reading this, she found you. Grief is not a lack of faith, Naomi.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: "Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning." (Psalm 30:5)

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: Wait for the morning. — your Savta

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Wait for the morning. It's hard to see one from here, Savta.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Every woman from the well is in this room. All but one. Where is Zilpah?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Not at the well. Not at her door. The widows have gone down to eat. So who lit a lamp in the weaving room?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Zilpah. Alone at Tabitha's loom. How long have you been sitting here?

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: Don't fuss, dear. Someone ought to mind the thread. It tangles if it's left.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: The whole town wept upstairs today. You weren't among them.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: And have them watch me do it? I know what they'd say. I taught them how to say it.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. No bangles tonight. And her hands won't keep still on that shawl.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: She wove this. Forty years ago. Nobody knows that. I let them think I bought it in Tyre.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Tabitha made your shawl? You never said you were close.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: I never said a great many true things. I was too busy with the other kind.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: I've a loaf, and nowhere to be. Tell me a true one, Zilpah.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: I was nineteen, and betrothed. A good family. The feast was a month away.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: Then a whisper started at the well. About me, and a man I had never spoken to.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: And nobody asked you.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: Not one. His family broke the betrothal. Mine put my bundle in the street.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: Only Tabitha came. She took me in and made me new clothes, so I could hold my head up.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: She never asked if it was true. She only measured my shoulders.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: And then you went back to the well.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: I swore no one would whisper about me again. So I made certain I was the one whispering.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: I became the thing that broke me.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: I know something about a story that isn't true. I'm not going anywhere, Zilpah.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: She was the only one who knew me. I never once thanked her out loud. Now who is there to tell?

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Nomi. The carters from Lydda say Peter is in their town. Half a day's walk, no more.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: Well now. Lydda is near. The brothers are agreed: we send two men and ask him to come.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Come for what, Elder? She's washed and laid out. What do we ask him for?

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: I don't know, child. I only know I cannot sit here and not ask.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: I'll go.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: You? You've not spent a night away from Joy since... not in two years.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: I know what a house is like, after. I'll go.

lines.speaker: marcus
lines.text: Then I'm the second. I walked that road with a toll seal once. Let me walk it for something better.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: Tell him only this: come to us, and do not delay.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: Papa never goes anywhere. Naomi, who is Peter? Can he fix things?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. I don't know. But if he comes he'll want a bed, and Simon has a room nobody sleeps in. That I can do.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: You came up the street dust to the knee, all three. Caleb. He went straight in?

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Straight in. We said, come and don't delay. He got up and came with us.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: We showed him the coats, every one she made us. Then he sent us all out. He was kneeling to pray as I shut the door.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: All of us out on the stair, and nobody breathing. He's praying. I can't make out the words.

lines.speaker: peter
lines.text: Tabitha, arise.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: ...The door. He's opening the door. Hannah, he has her by the hand.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: He is calling us in, the widows and all. Look. Look at her. She is alive.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: She's standing. She's looking at us. Oh, Tabitha!

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Wait for the morning, Savta said. ...I can't see. Somebody hold my basket.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: I carried the water to wash her. I saw her laid out. This morning she was at her own door, in the sun.

lines.speaker: dockworker2
lines.text: It's known in every street. Potters, tanners, the whole harbor. Nobody's done a stroke of work.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: Seventy-five years, little loaf, and I've no story to set beside it. Not one. I looked.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: You? Out of stories?

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: It's restful. I may sit down. ...Esther would have liked today.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: Demas! You've a crowd and no tale? Gather us close, man. Tell it!

lines.speaker: demas
lines.text: I... no. I wasn't on that stair, friends. I've nothing to add to it. Ask the widows. They were there.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: I'll tell what I saw and no more. She was dead. Peter knelt and prayed. He called us in, and she was alive.

lines.speaker: dockworker2
lines.text: Then tell me about this Lord of yours, widow. From the beginning. I've all day.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: The village folk in Simon's yard won't go home. They want to hear it again. They'll want water. Hm. The cistern.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: And Demas has gone grey as ash. A teller with no tale. What is it he can't bring himself to say?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Morning. I'll take the old well rope, if nobody wants it. Simon's drying racks are down to one rail.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: Take it, baker. ...Here's Zilpah. First time at the well since the hill. Easy, lads.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: Don't go, any of you. I've said a great deal at this stone. I've one thing more.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: Naomi. I asked about Roman houses with a smile on my face. Then I passed the Caesarea tale on. Gladly.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: I knew what a whisper does to a woman. Better than anyone here. I am asking you to forgive me.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: I forgive you, Zilpah.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: ...That's all? No speech, dear?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. I'm a baker. I keep things short.

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: Elder. And Marcus, when he's in from the boats. I said it of each of you, here, where it would carry. I ask the same.

lines.speaker: amos
lines.text: Well now. Asked and given. There's still room on that bench, Zilpah.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.text: Tabitha's tunics for the widows are washed and wet. Will you help me carry them down to Simon's racks?

lines.speaker: zilpah
lines.text: To the tanner's house? ...Yes. Give me the heavy end. And somebody tell me if I start talking.

lines.speaker: dockworker
lines.text: So the man of God sleeps at the tanner's. Hides and lime. A holy man, under that roof?

lines.speaker: dockworker2
lines.text: There are clean houses on the hill. People are saying he might have chosen better.

lines.speaker: simon
lines.text: They're not wrong about the smell. I told him so myself. He stayed anyway.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Then your doorstep shouldn't rock under him. Hold the bar, Simon. This stone comes up.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: A potsherd, flat in the sand. Savta. You came down here too?

lines.speaker: simon
lines.text: Every week, with bread. She'd sit on that step and say the sea air did her good.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: People hold their noses at this house. Holy things happen in the places people hold their noses at.

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: The Lord came "to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning," (Isaiah 61:3)

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: "the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness." (Isaiah 61:3)

lines.speaker: esther
lines.text: Tabitha sewed that verse into everything she ever made. — your Savta

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Beauty for ashes. Hm. Then this house gets a level step, a swept roof and a lamp. I'm staying, Joppa.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: I swept the whole roof! And the stair. And I found a crab. Simon says the crab may stay.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Mats down, water jar filled, and a breeze off the sea. Best room in the house, Simon.

lines.speaker: simon
lines.text: No guest ever stayed in my house past one night. He has stayed many days. I've stopped counting.

lines.speaker: peter
lines.text: Peace, friends. Is that bread? I could smell it from the street.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Barley loaves, still warm. I'm Naomi. I bake. It's all I know to do for a guest.

lines.speaker: peter
lines.text: Thank you, Naomi. I was a fisherman. Warm bread at noon is no small thing.

lines.speaker: silas
lines.text: A fisherman! Cast net or drag? Now, that reminds me of the year the fish swam backward—

lines.speaker: peter
lines.text: Sit down, friend. I'd like to hear about that year.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Hm. The first man in Joppa to ask for the whole story. Silas may never stop.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: Tabitha was dead and now she isn't. Hannah said. Naomi... could that happen for anybody?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Joy. ...Come and help me with the basket, little one.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Oil in the niche and a wick that holds. Now Simon's gate has a light, same as any house on the hill.

lines.speaker: caleb
lines.text: Hinge is sound too. Joy. Home. It's late.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: In a minute, Papa. I have to ask him something first.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Joy, wait. He's at his supper—

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: Peter. My mama died in the sea. Two years ago. Can you bring her back too?

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: He's set down his bread. He's come down to her height, eye to eye. He hasn't said a word.

lines.speaker: joy
lines.text: Her name is Leah. Papa knows the place. He could show you.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Caleb—

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: Gone. Out the gate without a word. His tools are still on the step. Caleb never leaves his tools.

lines.speaker: naomi
lines.text: And across the street, in my new lamplight, Demas. He heard it all. He saw me look. He looked away.
